title: cs-codex-turn reports a turn the provider ended with an error as a completed turn
foundBy: session agent operating two eight-member campaigns side by side on one host, reading every member's own CLI session records and the lender containers' logs after both campaigns had ended
details:
**What happened.** Across two campaigns, 23 of 41 codex turns were ended by the provider: 21 on the key's tokens-per-minute limit and 2 on *"Selected model is at capacity"*. In the rollout JSONL each of those turns ends with a `task_complete` event whose `last_agent_message` is `null` and whose `error.message` carries the provider's text. `cs-codex-turn` exited 0 for every one of them.

**Why.** The driver's completion test is a count: it waits until the rollout holds more `task_complete` events than it did before the prompt was submitted, and then reports success. It never reads the event. Its documented exit codes are *0 ok, 2 turn timed out/stalled, 3 launch/setup failure, 1 usage* — there is no code for a turn that failed, so a caller cannot tell a model that finished from a provider that refused.

**The precedent is in the same directory.** `cs-opencode-turn` already treats this as its own case: its header says provider-side API errors *"surface only on the session's"* record, it runs a post-check that is *"REQUIRED even on exit 0"*, and it exits **5, turn failed**. `cs-codex-turn` has no equivalent. Neither does `cs-claude-turn` (*0 ok, 2 turn timed out, 3 launch/setup failure, 1 usage/other*), which was not exercised by a provider error here and is named only because it has the same shape.

**What it costs downstream.** A campaign harness that sees a finished turn and no reply concludes the member stopped, and answers with a continue and then a restart, each of which re-sends the member's whole context into the limit that ended the turn. Three healthy members were written off as stuck that way. That half is filed in the campaign ledger as SAC-034, and the missing reason as SAC-035; this record is the place the reason is first lost.

**How to reproduce.** Point `OPENAI_BASE_URL` at a stub that answers every model call with HTTP 429 and a rate-limit body, run one prompt through `cs-codex-turn`, and wait out codex's retries. Expected today: exit status 0, with the rollout's last `task_complete` carrying an `error`. Described from the observed records and from reading the driver; not yet run against a stub.

**What would fix it.** Read the `task_complete` event the driver was waiting for. If it carries an `error`, exit with a failed-turn code as `cs-opencode-turn` does, print the provider's message on stderr, and — better — classify it (throttled, at capacity, unauthorized, context too long, other) on a line a caller can parse, including the provider's retry-after when it gives one.
